messages:
maya: kicking off a short PRD thread for Dedicated capacity sizing + SLA + autoscale. goal: ship an acceptance checklist + clear edge cases by EOW.
kevin: SGTM. do we have target customers to scope the throughput curves?
maya: primary customers: search-ranking SaaS (steady qps), and chat app with spiky traffic. ask: 99.9% availability SLA, 95th p99 token latency < 350ms for short responses.
carla: small note: 99.9% across multi-tenant shared pools is tricky. we should define SLA tiers (gold/silver/bronze) and map to reserved pools vs burst.
john: agree. suggest these mappings: gold -> dedicated reserved pool (pinned), silver -> reserved with warm pool + autoscale, bronze -> best-effort burst.
maya: acceptance criteria draft (high level):
- SLA: gold 99.9% availability, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 400ms under committed load.
- Throughput: list of sizing formulas per model class (small/med/large).
- Autoscale: scale-up within 60s for 2x sustained increase, scale-down with 15m cooldown.
- Rollout: canary 5% traffic, 15 minute watch with health metrics pass.
kevin: raw throughput numbers to convert to fleet size: we estimate 1 A100-80GB can sustain ~2200 short-gen tokens/s with batching tuned for chat workloads. for long-seq workloads reduce by ~40%.
sam: can we express configs as a table for the PRD? e.g., model class -> tokens/s -> recommended GPUs -> warm pool size.
maya: yes, we'll add a table in PRD. please propose numbers.
kevin: quick proposal: small models (<=3B): 5k tokens/s -> 4 gpu per 10k qps bucket; med models (7-13B): 2k tokens/s; large (70B+): 400 tokens/s. warm pool target = 10% of committed fleet, min 2 nodes.
carla: edge cases to call out: preemptible instances being reclaimed -> need graceful sharding fallback, and 'noisy neighbor' detection for degraded latency.
john: action: implement routing fallback policy: if a node's p95 > 2x baseline for 30s mark as degraded and route to spare pool. infra-bot: noted. creating ticket INF-7823.
maya: acceptance test ideas:
- load test: run 1.5x committed qps for 20m, check no dropped requests and SLA math holds.
- cold start test: simulate full fleet power-cycle, measure time to reach 80% of baseline throughput.
- failover test: kill 10% of nodes and verify routing/fallback keeps success rate >= SLA.
kevin: autoscale policy details: use predictive scale-up (based on 1m qps trend) plus reactive immediate spin-up for spike events. also cap burst to 2x committed capacity.
sam: for the PRD acceptance criteria, can we add measurable metrics + thresholds? e.g., lost requests <= 0.1% during 1.5x load, retry success within 2 attempts >= 99.5%.
carla: will require observability: per-route latency histograms, per-node health, queue depth, batch sizes. add tracing hooks for request routing.
maya: good. who can own the SLO verification harness?
kevin: eng-runtime can own load tests and harness. john/eng-platform to own rollout automation and routing fallback. carla to write SLO/alerting runbooks.
maya: risk register (short bullets):
- underestimated token/s per GPU -> capacity shortfall. mitigation: conservative initial buffer + fast canary.
- warm pool cost -> negotiate minimums with sales for committed tiers.
- cross-tenant interference -> strict isolation for gold tier.
anna: from customer-ops: also include metrics customers can see in console (token cost, p95 latency, outage timeline). transparency matters.
sam: also capture billing/overage behavior when autoscaling past commit. limit caps and explicit alert to the customer.
kevin: quick config example to include in PRD:
```
commit: 1000 rps
burst_cap: 2000 rps
warm_pool: 10 nodes
scale_up_policy:
  reactive: +1 node per 200 rps sustained in 30s\  predictive: lookahead 60s using EWMA
scale_down_policy:
  cooldown: 900s
```
maya: love the config sketch. final asks before I draft: any missing edge cases?
john: multi-region failover needs explicit SLOs if region outage occurs. define cross-region fallback latency penalty and data residency constraints.
carla: don't forget thundering herd on cold caches (kv/prefix caches). add staggered warm-up and jitter.
kevin: for acceptance: include synthetic canary prompts that exercise worst-case decoder paths and measure p99 token time.
maya: ok i'll assemble the PRD with these parts: goals, mapping table, sizing formulas, autoscale config, rollout plan, tests, runbooks, customer-visible metrics, risk register. aim to share draft tomorrow AM.
sam: can we schedule 30m review Fri after draft?
maya: scheduled. ping me if anything else. :thumbsup:
